title: Swift Response
text: “So that’s me from the previous loop, huh… Now I’m curious what kind of guy I was.”
“That would be Father, who told Ren and Itsuki about the kingdom’s conspiracy before the false charges could take hold, shook it off, and set his sights on Faubrey, indeed.”
“Wow. Though it seems tricky to pull that off starting from here.”

There was much I wished to discuss, but what should be done from here on, I wondered? I needed to sort out what had to be done after rescuing Father, indeed. Was there some other pressing matter I ought to prioritize… something I needed to recall? Tiger Girl flitted across my mind, but… well, surely that was just my imagination. Right, indeed. Rescuing Big Sister had to come next. Either way, there was apparently a way to meet her regardless. It felt like the situation regarding Big Sister’s friend had grown rather dangerous. Which meant I needed to hurry. My stock of medicine wouldn’t heal her immediately, but regardless, something had to be done, I say. Let me ask the Siltvelt envoy.
“For the time being, there’s something I’d like to do next—could we possibly secure some medicine? It’s just for emergency measures; I’ll pay for the treatment afterward, indeed.”
“What is it you intend to do?”
“Rescue those whose lives will soon be lost unless saved, and whose absence would otherwise complicate our reunion, I say.”
“So it’s something you have to prioritize because of your knowledge of the future. In situations like this, I think it’s usually best to move as quickly as possible—what do you think?”
“As expected of Father! Just so, indeed.”

We were in a situation where we couldn’t rely on backup from the Queen or anyone like that. Since I’d been told not to act by the optimal solution, I decided not to depend on the Queen and instead ask the Siltvelt envoy for the bare minimum of cooperation.
“Understood. Then let us consult with whatever domestic contacts might be able to help.”

And so it seemed the Siltvelt envoy went off to speak with someone, heading toward a rather shady district in the town beneath Melromarc Castle. The envoy discussed various matters there. While I accompanied them, the portal’s cooldown finally passed.
“Well then, let’s be off at once, indeed.”
“I should come along too, right?”
“Indeed so.”
Since Father had been reinforced together with Kuro-chan, he should be able to withstand minor attacks without so much as flinching, I say.
“I’d like Kuro-chan to come along as an escort, indeed.”
“Okaaay!”
Now then… I turned to face the Siltvelt envoy.
“Will you be coming as well?”
“Yes. I have no idea what sort of events await, but I have been entrusted with the duty of escorting Shield Hero-sama.”

Since I had forcibly canceled the trip to Siltvelt, I supposed showing them properly was the only way to satisfy them. Still, judging from experience across previous loops, this was someone who would understand once shown Big Sister and the others’ circumstances.
“Very well, indeed. But… someone will need to watch over the remaining Filolial-samas in our absence.”
“Rest assured. My subordinates will see to their care.”
“That’s most reassuring, indeed. Well, we should be back soon enough, so it should be fine. Now then, let us depart at once, indeed.”

And so, having made my preparations, I flew straight to the noble’s mansion in the large town where Big Sister and the others were being held captive. I slipped in swiftly under stealth. Since Kuro-chan was with us this time, I had Father and the others ride on her back for this operation. It was a square mansion with a courtyard.
“Kuro-chan, let’s leap in all at once and land in the courtyard, indeed.”
“Okaaay. Naofumi and the others, hold on tight now.”
“Right. I’ll leave it to you.”
And so, with Kuro-chan’s help, Father and the others landed safely in the courtyard. By layering Cloaking Lance with Fire Mirage, we managed to infiltrate quietly, indeed.
“Heh heh… the silent intruder ＜Assassin＞ slips through the darkness into the stronghold of the Order of Light.”
This was, apparently, proof that Kuro-chan was a Filolial-sama just like Black Thunder.
“How should I put it… Kuro-chan’s got quite the personality once she starts talking, huh?”
“Indeed, I say.”
“Moto, is Kuro’s destined one ＜Destiny＞ here?”
“Unfortunately, not here, indeed.”
It still wasn’t the time to introduce her to Ren, I supposed.
“Awww.”

With that, we continued on toward the mansion’s basement, still cloaked. Along the way there was a locked door, which of course we simply smashed through without hesitation, indeed. But here, Kuro-chan’s feet came to a stop.
“What’s wrong, Kuro-chan?”
“Something feels bad.”
“Filolial-samas are quite sensitive, indeed.”
“…Judging by the location, this isn’t exactly a wholesome place. Likely the seedier side of Melromarc’s people.”

The Siltvelt envoy seemed to have some idea of what lay ahead. Kuro-chan, sensing the unpleasant presence, furrowed her brow slightly, but pressed forward all the same. Other Filolial-samas might have hesitated to approach, but Kuro-chan—Black Thunder—seemed to be the type unfazed by this sort of thing. Come to think of it, Black Thunder had always approached Hou-kun without hesitation. It was Ark she seemed to have trouble with.

Since receiving advice, she and Ark had been talking more. I recalled how excited she’d gotten cheering Ark on when watching him vanish into the night and reappear behind an opponent. Come to think of it, Ark had mentioned that Black Thunder wanted to use dark magic but couldn’t, and that this troubled her. And apparently what Black Thunder truly preferred was to carry an aged Ren on her back and run about heroically. As I mused on such things while advancing quietly…
“So it really is…”

The Siltvelt envoy pressed a hand over their mouth. They’d caught the foul odor. Pressing onward… there was Big Sister, strung up. However, no noble was present. It seemed we’d arrived outside of torture hours—simply a matter of timing, I supposed.
“That’s…”
Father fell speechless. There before him was young Big Sister, in the very midst of being tortured.
“…To do such cruel things to a mere child, those Melromarc scum.”
The Siltvelt envoy clenched their fists tight, brow furrowed deeply.
“Uuu…”

Kuro-chan seemed to recoil hard at the sheer horror of the state before her. Judging things by seeing them firsthand with her own eyes—that, I think, was Kuro-chan’s, Black Thunder’s, great strength. I sliced through the cage’s lock without further delay. With a creak, I opened the cage door, slipped inside, and released the cloak. Disarming the trigger lever, I freed Big Sister—dazed as she was—from the chains binding her.
“Are you all right? Stay with me.”
Father supported Big Sister and laid her down gently.
“Will warmth help her feel better? Should Kuro warm her up with fluffy feathers?”
Kuro-chan settled down quietly beside the reclining Big Sister and draped her feathers over her.
“Ahh…”
She was weaker than she’d been in the loop where the Queen had witnessed this scene. I’d taken a bit too much time.
“You are…”
“Never mind that for now—let me focus on treating you first. Hey, please, treat this child.”
“There’s a friend of mine in an even worse state than me.”
“I understand, indeed. Since my medicine supply is a bit uncertain, I’ll prioritize treating external injuries first, I say.”

I released Al Liberation Fireheal X around us. It made me a little anxious, but Big Sister’s friend should be here somewhere too, suffering from illness. Wound treatment and illness called for different remedies, but since it could also restore vitality, it should serve well enough as emergency first aid. Checking the cell further, I found Big Sister’s friend there as well.
“Haah… haah…”
Her breathing was unstable. Restoring her vitality had to take priority, or things would turn dire.
“This is dreadful…”
“Have this child take the medicine, indeed.”
“Yes.”

I took the medicine from the Siltvelt envoy and tried to get Big Sister’s friend to drink it, but… she was so weakened she lacked even the strength to swallow. In times like this, there was only one thing to do.
“Moto, lend Kuro that medicine—”

Kuro-chan transformed into her angelic form, took the medicine from my hands, held it in her own mouth, and poured it directly into Big Sister’s friend’s mouth. Oh, that was exactly what I’d been about to do myself, but Kuro-chan certainly didn’t hesitate, I say. Incidentally, Filolial-samas often feed their chicks this very way, so there was no reservation involved at all.
The Difference Between Kuro and Black Thunder
